children: A broad selloff in technology stocks gathered pace this week, with chipmakers, cloud computing groups, cybersecurity companies and software providers all sharply lower. Several of the sector’s biggest names lost billions of dollars in market value after reporting earnings or issuing forecasts that disappointed investors
The iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF
fell 5.52% for the week, while the Dow Jones U.S. Software Index lost more than 3%. The Nasdaq Composite declined 1.95%, as of mid-day Friday.
Star analyst Dan Ives described the week as “absolutely brutal” for technology investors, saying the disruption from AI was becoming increasingly visible in corporate earnings.
Alphabet

suffered its biggest one-day percentage decline on record on Thursday, falling as much as 13% and wiping out roughly $500B in market value. Google reported a rare earnings miss on slower growth in search advertising and a sharp increase in AI spending.
Intel

shares plunged about 30% on Friday after the chipmaker issued a fourth-quarter forecast well below Wall Street expectations, warning that weakness in the personal computer market could persist through the first half of 2027.
INTC decline also dragged down semiconductor stocks. The PHLX Semiconductor Sector index
fell 9%. AMD
dropped 11%, Broadcom
and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing
each fell 6%, and Micron
and Nvidia
each lost 5%. SanDisk
shares fell 12% on Friday despite reporting better-than-expected quarterly results and issuing stronger guidance and an eight-for-one stock split.
Amazon
shares shed roughly 7% following its earnings report, as its aggressive investment plans overshadowed growth in its cloud computing business. Microsoft
offered a relative bright spot, with shares down about just 2% since its results. Though it moved to raise $25B through a bond offering.
ServiceNow

shares tumbled more than 25% on Thursday after the enterprise software company issued a weaker-than-expected forecast for subscription growth, reviving concerns about the potential impact of AI on traditional software businesses.
Fortinet

shares plunged about 27%. Although the company beat third-quarter earnings and revenue estimates, investors were disappointed by slower product revenue growth and a reduction in its full-year services revenue outlook.
Selloff spread to other software and cybersecurity companies, with Zscaler
falling 7.5%, Okta losing 7.1%, Rubrik declining 5.3%, Palo Alto Networks dropping 5%, Cloudflare shedding 4.9%, CrowdStrike falling 4.6% and SentinelOne losing 3.5%, since Thursday. Twilio
shares tumbled 19% on Friday despite the company beating third-quarter earnings and revenue estimates, but analysts called its smaller-than-expected beat.
The tech sell-off represented a moment for long thought rather than a full market reckoning, according to Matt Orton, chief market strategist at Raymond James.

"This pivotal tech earnings week has been a tale of two cities for tech investors…bringing a painful week to the tech bulls although the underlying drivers of the AI Revolution are even more defined going forward in our view," Ives said.

title: Alphabet’s record plunge, Intel’s 30% collapse: tech’s brutal week of reckoning
